mode: Ordinary persistent InnoDB with stock foreign_key_checks=1, utf8mb4 and empty sql_mode.

Schema/ForeignKey/Add/AddForeignKeys.role: One completed ALTER TABLE group of native persistent InnoDB foreign-key additions.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/AddForeignKeys.structure: Absolute child table, detached ordered declarations, effective algorithm, lock, legacy IGNORE and release. The completed value includes the exact removed implicit physical key names.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/AddForeignKeys.conditions: Validate native schema symbol allocation, physical generated keys and earlier parent support from complete original facts. Validate release, scope and lock before publication.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/AddForeignKeys.meaning: Declare each ordered child-parent reference and its physical key effect. Keep the independent parent update and delete effects and exact catalog metadata. Native generated child keys can replace prior eligible implicit keys. Preserve that closed effect and keep the original catalog outside the value.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/AddForeignKeys.sql: Emit the native ALTER owner, checked group and effective policy.

Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyAddition.role: One resolved native constraint relative to its enclosing child table.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyAddition.structure: Absolute parent, exact symbol and origin, checked ordered pairs and effect variant, optional named and created physical index.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyAddition.conditions: One through sixteen paired fields, distinct on each side, resolved parent and matching nullability for SET NULL. The enclosing group checks symbols and physical effects.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyAddition.meaning: Introduce a distinct native foreign key on the selected parent field coordinates, with an explicit generated physical index effect when applicable.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyAddition.sql: Emit ADD FOREIGN KEY, explicit symbol or native generation, paired field lists, and declarative effects.

Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyPair.role: One ordered native child and parent field pair.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyPair.structure: Decoded relative physical identifiers, native integer width and sign, child nullability and ordered physical direction.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyPair.conditions: Both identifiers are within the native physical column namespace. The pairing uses one native integer domain and the full field on each side.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyPair.meaning: Compare two external field values in the fixed integer domain, and use the child direction when a physical supporting index is created.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyPair.sql: Emit both quoted identifiers in the two list positions and the selected child direction.

Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyEffects.role: Foreign-key catalog MATCH metadata and separate parent-row event actions.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyEffects.structure: Closed update action, delete action and MATCH variant.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyEffects.conditions: The owner and release check capability. SET NULL requires each referenced child field to be nullable.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyEffects.meaning: Use independent parent update and delete effects and preserve exact catalog metadata. All admitted match variants allow child rows containing a NULL key field.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyEffects.sql: Emit the retained MATCH metadata and the two independently ordered event choices.

Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyAction.role: The native declared action for one referenced row event.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyAction.structure: Closed cases RESTRICT, NO ACTION, CASCADE, SET NULL and SET DEFAULT.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyAction.conditions: The enclosing native release and child field layout check admissibility.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyAction.meaning: CASCADE and SET NULL change the corresponding child rows. Under this InnoDB profile RESTRICT, NO ACTION and admitted SET DEFAULT refuse changes to a referenced parent row.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyAction.sql: Emit the fixed native action token.

Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyMatch.role: The retained native MATCH catalog metadata.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyMatch.structure: Closed absent, FULL and PARTIAL variants.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyMatch.conditions: Established by the native release and matched against the declared references.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyMatch.meaning: Preserve catalog metadata independently of child partial-NULL admission.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/ForeignKeyMatch.sql: Emit FULL or PARTIAL when requested by the effective native metadata.

Schema/ForeignKey/Add/Catalog/ForeignKey.role: A checked original native constraint in the transient construction input.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/Catalog/ForeignKey.structure: Absolute persistent owner and decoded physical symbol.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/Catalog/ForeignKey.conditions: A valid physical foreign-key symbol is limited to 64 BMP characters. The owning statement checks native namespace uniqueness.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/Catalog/ForeignKey.meaning: Occupy one exact database-level constraint identity and its eligible owner-sequence marker.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/Catalog/ForeignKey.sql: Used by the group to compute its emitted constraint naming policy.

Schema/ForeignKey/Add/Catalog/ForeignKey.role: A checked original physical key placement used by construction.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/Catalog/ForeignKey.structure: Absolute physical key identity, detached ordered full prefix, completeness and native reference eligibility.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/Catalog/ForeignKey.conditions: Persistent owning table, unique ordered field identifiers and explicit prefix completeness. A native non-B-tree key can occupy a name without supplying an eligible field.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/Catalog/ForeignKey.meaning: Occupy one physical index name and, when eligible, support a resolved native ordered prefix.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/Catalog/ForeignKey.sql: Constrain creation and binding of the group. Original keys are external declarations.

Schema/ForeignKey/Add/Catalog/ForeignKey.role: One physical full field term in an original supporting key.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/Catalog/ForeignKey.structure: A decoded native field ID and immutable direction.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/Catalog/ForeignKey.conditions: The name is a full physical column name; the key validates its ordered placement.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/Catalog/ForeignKey.meaning: Supply the precise field and direction of one existing physical key term.
Schema/ForeignKey/Add/Catalog/ForeignKey.sql: Constrain the exact child-side key allocation and parent support; no additional declaration is emitted for this term.

observations: Exact persistent owners and parent column coordinates, order, and NULL effects
Native constraint names, metadata and matching logical rules
Original and resulting qualified physical keys with more than one pair, direction, and reuse versus allocation
Actual parent writes and child rows, including unresolved catalog refusal and data-dependent native rejection
Effective DDL transaction behavior and exact diagnostic categories
Observe no removed physical indexes in this declared original layout and check replacement explicitly in the separate exchange and replacement observations.
The separate native exchange schedule also exercises pure addition with equal and longer prior generated support.
negative: Exact native policy, legacy direction, legacy SET DEFAULT and SET NULL nullability refusals
Absent parent physical support including exact unique requirement since 8.4
Open, inconsistent, ambiguous, or unaccounted construction facts
A distinct native execution-time integrity refusal under a valid structural operation

evidence.P01: Observe resolved owner and persistent parent, exact ordered child-parent pairs, effective events, matching metadata, names and key effects.
evidence.P02: Require the original complete physical catalog and reject unsupported policy, field, key, symbol or event conditions in both routes.
evidence.P03: Interpret published typed immutable fields independently of the original syntax and declaration catalog.
evidence.P04: Derive exact original/support/new key placement, ordered constraints and event behavior from the closed declaration values.
evidence.P05: Verify fully detached typed child arrays, supported immutable parts and unreachable unvalidated restoration.
evidence.P06: Compare emitted and original ALTER with independently expected catalog, referential effects, rows and native DDL observations.

obligations.Q01: Audit closed typed construction plus exact local and boundary rejections.
obligations.Q02: Reconcile both public routes over the fixed product and all executed seeds and directed neighbors.
obligations.Q03: Check complete physical support, group order and symbol effects, including cross-database and same-field controls.
obligations.Q04: Compare exact physical metadata and row effects against native InnoDB. Recheck designated semantic faults.
obligations.Q05: Bind exact release ledgers, constructor and source receipts and both installed distribution paths.

faults: Resolve the wrong persistent parent in the current database.
Transpose the two effective parent-row actions.
Erase native MATCH metadata with unchanged rows.
Erase an observed partial-NULL insertion outcome.
trackedBeyondThisSlice: Generated and non-integer key field profiles, including observed decimal encodings and collation families
ALTER forms mixing addition with dropping or renaming native keys or constraints
Legacy length corner cases containing truncated protocol names and database-encoded identities
Outlier automatic ordinal wraparound and affected legacy temporary dictionary artifacts
Mode changes that allow InnoDB online addition under disabled referential checks
trust: Complete accurately interpreted native schema facts and the specified stock language profile
The future independent executable verifier, its native fixture environment and the human-reviewed protected reference
